question: The house I'm buying has a Pushmatic panel. Is that a problem, and what do I do before closing?
verdictConfirmed: Not a recalled product: CPSC's recall database has no Pushmatic record. The real questions are the panel's age and condition, and whether YOUR insurer accepts it -- get that answer in writing. Replacement breakers are still sold, so 'no parts' is not a reason on its own.

facts.claim: CPSC's public recall database returns no records for Pushmatic (we queried it on 2026-11-19). The same query for Challenger returns Challenger's 1988 GFCI breaker replacement program, which shows the search works.
facts.quote: GET https://www.saferproducts.gov/RestWebServices/Recall?format=json&ProductName=pushmatic -> 0 records; RecallTitle=pushmatic -> 0 records; ProductName=challenger -> 3 records incl. 1988-11-12 'Challenger Electrical Equipment Corp. Offers Replacement Program For 9000 GFCI C...'
facts.method: webfetch (our own API query; first-party observation)

facts.claim: Replacement breakers for Pushmatic panels are still sold: Connecticut Electric's UBIP line, described as classified for use in Pushmatic and Bulldog load centers, ETL listed.
facts.quote: Classified for use in Pushmatic and Bulldog load centers. ... Connecticut Electric replacement circuit breaker for Pushmatic circuit breakers. ... ETL Listed.

facts.claim: Florida's Citizens 4-point inspection form (Insp4pt 03 25) records the main panel's brand/model, panel age and year last updated, and says underwriting relies on the form to determine insurability. Describe the form; never write that a named insurer declines anything. The same form's Electrical 'Hazards Present' checklist includes scorching, corrosion and tripping breakers.

facts.claim: Pushmatic breakers are push buttons rather than toggle switches; the label may say Pushmatic, Bulldog or I-T-E.
facts.quote: These are the easiest to spot: instead of toggle switches, the breakers are rectangular push buttons. The label may say Pushmatic, Bulldog or I-T-E.
